A.reason: Cheap, cleanly re-testable on past finals logs, but it only re-selects among existing finalists and its core move is fitting the internal judge to the benchmark rater, which is Goodhart risk rather than better ideas.

B.reason: Raters see only cards, the deterministic checker plus verifier bounds invented claims, and the offline edited-vs-original rating rerun is the cleanest isolated test in the set; gain is capped because it fixes presentation, not idea quality.

C.reason: A 60-line scoring-only change with a clean offline replay, but the gain is conditional on the benchmark metric being best-of-3 (the card admits mean-of-3 loses by construction) and the cluster-shift tau is asserted, not fitted.

D.reason: The LUCB analogy is about identification, not improvement: refining ideas at the rank-3/4 boundary barely moves the quality of the delivered top 3, so +30-50% cost buys a marginal effect the card itself half-concedes via the germinal-centre caveat.

E.reason: Presupposes an executable-check ledger (Idea F) that does not exist in the described system, costs 1-2 weeks and 2x development tokens, and its primary outcome (falsified-claim rate) is a proxy that need not track rater preference.

F.reason: Tool-grounded critique is a real mechanism, but it needs a sandbox in the state machine, rests on an unverified 40% checkability assumption that fails for qualitative briefs like this one, and the outcome metric is its own proxy.

G.reason: Selecting from a strict superset of the baseline's candidates gives a floor whenever the internal judge correlates with raters and makes any multi-agent gain visible as displaced champions, at the cost of one extra single-agent run; the conservative 80% gate will often just yield ties.

H.reason: Zero extra tokens and a clean offline refit, but it needs ~300 internal votes on externally rated ideas and a reference distinct from the eval panel, and it can only improve selection among finalists, not the finalists themselves.

I.reason: Sensible residual design that degrades to today's BT with few labels, but ~150 labels across heterogeneous briefs for ~10 features is thin, labelling doubles panel cost, and learning from panel verdicts risks encoding the panel's biases.

J.reason: Depends on a contest loop that does not exist, needs ~50 brief runs to detect a 10-point effect on an in-loop proxy (child-beats-parent under the same judge), and its own failure list concedes the effect may be undetectable.

K.reason: It exploits the one thing a lone agent lacks, independent adversarial loss reasons, then makes revision monotone via a different-family two-order gate with length matching, and the no-reasons control arm isolates the conditioning effect at +25% cost.
